title: Understand what your compiler did
blurb: From the source you wrote to the instructions that ran, with nothing taken on faith.
who: You read assembly occasionally and mostly guess. You want to stop guessing.

stages.title: The instruction set, for real
stages.why: Not the tutorial version. The registers, how an address is formed, what a system call actually is, and what a linker leaves behind.

stages.title: Why the same instructions run at different speeds
stages.why: Two programs with identical instruction counts differ by ten times, and the reason is never in the listing.

stages.title: The compiler's own middle
stages.why: The representation an optimiser actually works on, how instructions get chosen, and what a debugger has to be told to make any of it legible.

stages.title: Measuring instead of believing
stages.why: The last unit is the one that makes the rest usable: how to find out, rather than reason about, which of two versions is faster.
